_source: Hand-verified during research: each state's own Secretary of State (or equivalent) official candidate database, checked directly (live network inspection of the real API/page, not scraped from a third party like Ballotpedia) for a machine-readable, no-key, official source that distinguishes a real confirmed general-election candidate from an FEC filer who lost their primary or runoff.
_method: A state with no entry here is simply not yet covered — the ballot page falls back to its prior behavior (every active FEC filer shown) for that state, same as any other partial-coverage feature in this app (ballot measures, county-district crosswalk). This file only ever ADDS accuracy, never removes a state's chance at showing candidates.

CO.source_name: Colorado Secretary of State (Clarity Election Night Reporting)
CO.description: Official statewide results feed, verified live 2026-08-12 against the real 2026 primary (EID 126592): elections.json -> current_ver.txt -> json/sum.json, no API key or auth. All 18 federal contests (8 districts x 2 parties, plus both Senate primaries) parse cleanly. Ground-truthed against the CO-01 Democratic primary, where the feed shows Melat Kiros 83,855 (53.2%) defeating 15-term incumbent Diana DeGette 62,715 with Wanda James third — matching what actually happened on 2026-06-30. runoff_threshold_pct is null because Colorado awards its primary to the plurality leader outright, so the top vote-getter IS the nominee; a runoff state must set this or its runoff-bound leader would be mislabeled.

CA.source_name: California Secretary of State (certified Statement of Vote)
CA.description: Certified Statement of Vote workbook for voter-nominated (top-two) offices, verified live 2026-08-15: county-level rows carrying Contest Name ('United States Representative District 10'), Candidate Name, Party Name and Vote Total, read with the standard library since an xlsx is a zip of XML and no Excel dependency is warranted. All 52 congressional districts are present; California has no Senate seat on the 2026 ballot. advance_count is 2 because California runs a single all-party primary and sends the TOP TWO to the general regardless of party — modelling it as one nominee per party would silently drop a real ballot option, including the same-party runoffs California regularly produces. runoff_threshold_pct is null: there is no runoff, the top two simply advance.

WA.source_name: Washington Secretary of State (official results portal)
WA.description: Same portal software as Georgia's, reached through the identical sos_api_report discovery — which is the whole point of the vendor-adapter split: Washington cost a config entry, not a module. Verified live 2026-08-15 (publicElectionId 20260804, 'U.S. Representative - Congressional District N', 976 rows). advance_count is 2: Washington is a top-two state like California, and its party column is free-text candidate PREFERENCE ('Prefers Cascade Democrat Party', 'Prefers No Kings Party'), which is only ever a tiebreak here, never the match signal. require_official is set because Washington votes by mail and was still counting on 2026-08-15 — isOfficialResults was false, so this state correctly confirms nobody until certification on 2026-08-18, then lights up on its own. settle_days is the failsafe under that gate: Utah proved the portal's official flag is not reliably flipped, so a certified-but-unflagged election still counts once it is 30 days past. No Washington Senate seat is on the 2026 ballot.

VA.source_name: Virginia Department of Elections (official results portal)
VA.description: Third state on the same Enhanced Voting portal as Georgia and Washington, so again a config entry rather than a module. Two things make Virginia different, and both are why it waited: it runs its Democratic and Republican primaries as two SEPARATE elections on the same day (publicElectionIds 2026-August-Democratic-Primary and 2026-August-Republican-Primary, both 2026-08-04), hence a list of election patterns; and its federal label is 'Member, House of Representatives (2nd District)' with no 'U.S.' prefix, which parse_office deliberately refuses so a state lower chamber can't slip through — the export's own DistrictType == 'congressional' column is the discriminator instead. Verified live 2026-08-16 against the real CSVs: Elaine Luria taking the VA-02 Democratic primary, Don Beyer VA-08, Tom Perriello VA-05. Virginia nominates on a plurality, so there is no runoff threshold. require_official is set and both primaries were still uncertified 12 days out, so Virginia confirms nobody until the state board certifies, then lights up on its own — or, under settle_days, 30 days out if this portal never flips its official flag (Utah's never did). Only contested races appear in these files — an unopposed nominee is simply absent, and that seat keeps the FEC-filer fallback.

UT.source_name: Utah Lieutenant Governor's Office (official results portal)
UT.description: Fourth state on the Enhanced Voting portal, found on 2026-08-16 by probing /results/public/ across state results hosts — pure config, no code. Verified live against the real 2026-06-23 primary workbook: Ben McAdams taking the UT-01 Democratic primary, Blake Moore UT-02 and Celeste Maloy UT-03 on the Republican side (district numbers are the post-2026-redistricting map, which is exactly why they come from the state's own feed rather than being inferred). Only 3 federal contests exist — Utah's convention/signature path means most seats never reach a primary ballot, and an unopposed nominee is simply absent here. The name pattern excludes Utah's odd-year MUNICIPAL primary. Utah is why settle_days exists: this primary was canvassed and certified on 2026-07-22, its signed state canvass report is published on this very portal, and isOfficialResults was STILL false a month later — so require_official alone would have confirmed nobody here forever.

GA.source_name: Georgia Secretary of State (official results portal)
GA.description: Official statewide totals workbook, discovered live 2026-08-15 through the portal's own API rather than any hardcoded path: jurisdictions/Georgia lists every election (publicElectionId 'GeneralPrimary51926' for the 2026-05-19 General Primary) plus the portal id, the election document names its report blobs, and the blob GUID — which changes on every republish — is read each run. 30 federal contests. Georgia nominates on a majority, so runoff_threshold_pct is 50 AND the 2026-06-16 General Primary Runoff is fetched as a second stage that overrides the primary for every race it decides; without that merge the runoff seats would stay permanently unconfirmed. exclude_choices drops the per-contest 'Total Votes' summary row, which sits in the same shape as a candidate and would otherwise double the denominator and win uncontested races outright.

NC.source_name: North Carolina State Board of Elections (public results export)
NC.description: Official statewide precinct-results export, verified live 2026-08-12 against the real 2026-03-03 primary: the S3 listing at dl.ncsbe.gov resolves ENRS/2026 -> results_pct_20260303.zip (1.4 MB, 103,517 rows, 49,884 federal) with no key or auth, yielding 21 federal contests. Ground-truthed on Virginia Foxx taking NC-05 Republican with 74.5% and Valerie Foushee NC-04 Democratic with 49.2%. runoff_threshold_pct is 30 because North Carolina nominates on 30%+1 and sends anything below to a second primary — NC-01 Republican was won on 39.5%, which clears it, but a sub-30% leader must not be confirmed while a second primary is still possible.

TX.source_name: Texas Secretary of State (Civix Candidate Bio Portal)
TX.description: Official statewide candidate database, verified live via network inspection (not scraping the rendered Angular SPA): GET .../getElectionsByYear/{year} to find the current cycle's 'GE' (General Election) id, then POST .../findQualifiedCandidates with that id. cdOfficeType='FD' isolates federal races; txOfficeName parses to office+district ('U. S. SENATOR' / 'U. S. REPRESENTATIVE DISTRICT N'); cdFilingStatus='CG' ('Candidate in the General Election') is the authoritative confirmed-nominee flag, verified against known-correct 2026 ground truth (Paxton beat Cornyn in the May runoff; Paxton alone carries CG, Cornyn is absent from the GE-scoped query entirely). No API key, no auth.
